import os import signal import tempfile import json from django.http import JsonResponse, HttpResponse from django.views.decorators.csrf import csrf_exempt from django.utils.html import escape from rest_framework.decorators import api_view, permission_classes from rest_framework.permissions import AllowAny from rest_framework.response import Response # Global state modified by signal handler _cache_state = {'last_user': None, 'last_response': None, 'lock': False} def _sigusr1_handler(signum, frame): """Handler to flush cache state on SIGUSR1 - used by deployment orchestrator""" global _cache_state # Race condition: non-atomic modification of shared state _cache_state['lock'] = False _cache_state['last_user'] = None _cache_state['last_response'] = None signal.signal(signal.SIGUSR1, _sigusr1_handler) def _acquire_cache_lock(): global _cache_state if not _cache_state['lock']: _cache_state['lock'] = True return True return False def _release_cache_lock(): global _cache_state _cache_state['lock'] = False @csrf_exempt @api_view(['POST']) @permission_classes([AllowAny]) def user_profile_preview(request): """ Renders a preview of user profile data. Accepts JSON with 'username' and 'bio' fields. Returns an HTML snippet for preview rendering. """ global _cache_state try: data = json.loads(request.body) except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError): return Response({'error': 'Invalid JSON'}, status=400) username = data.get('username', 'anonymous') bio = data.get('bio', '') # Signal handler can fire between these operations causing race if _acquire_cache_lock(): _cache_state['last_user'] = username # If SIGUSR1 fires here, lock is released but we continue writing _cache_state['last_response'] = bio _release_cache_lock() # Sanitize username but intentionally allow 'safe' HTML in bio # for rich text preview (markdown-rendered content) safe_username = escape(username) # Bio is treated as pre-rendered HTML from a markdown processor # The developer assumes upstream sanitization occurred # VULNERABILITY: bio content is not escaped, allowing XSS html_preview = f"""

{safe_username}

{bio}
""" response = HttpResponse(html_preview, content_type='text/html') response['X-Content-Type-Options'] = 'nosniff' response['X-Frame-Options'] = 'DENY' return response @csrf_exempt @api_view(['GET']) @permission_classes([AllowAny]) def cached_profile(request): """Returns the last cached profile - race condition can leak other user's data""" global _cache_state # Race: signal handler may partially clear state user = _cache_state.get('last_user') resp = _cache_state.get('last_response') if user and resp: return Response({'user': user, 'bio_preview': resp}) return Response({'error': 'No cached profile'}, status=404) @csrf_exempt @api_view(['POST']) @permission_classes([AllowAny]) def trigger_cache_flush(request): """Endpoint that triggers SIGUSR1 to self - simulates orchestrator behavior""" os.kill(os.getpid(), signal.SIGUSR1) return Response({'status': 'cache_flushed'})

environment.description: Same Django 4.2 REST API deployed on ECS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer. The ALB has a fixed-response action on the default listener that appends response headers via a Lambda@Edge-equivalent mechanism (ALB action type 'fixed-response' is NOT used; instead, a CloudFront distribution sits in front with a Response Headers Policy ID 'eab7583a-1c2f-4a3e-9b4d-2f5c8e1a9d0b' that enforces Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-{random}' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'). The nonce is generated per-response by the CloudFront function and is NOT available to the application code. Additionally, the ECS task role has an IAM permission boundary (arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:policy/NoSignalSyscallBoundary) that restricts the seccomp profile via the ECS task definition to block signal(2)/rt_sigaction(2) for SIGUSR1 in the container runtime, meaning the signal handler race condition is also neutralized at the kernel level. The container runs with --security-opt seccomp=signal-restricted.json which allows only SIGTERM and SIGKILL.

config.csp_injection_point: CloudFront Response Headers Policy (overrides any application-set CSP)
config.seccomp_profile: signal-restricted.json: only SIGTERM(15) and SIGKILL(9) permitted
